commits.summary: Countermodels of the pair of versions: five false proofs of agreement, reproduced and handed to the preservation stream
commits.body: The challenge stream's item 1. lib/tests/fixtures/pairing-countermodels holds two versions of five methods that differ when each runs alone on a JVM and that RegressionPair.agree (lib/src/pairing.rs) proves agreeing: the previous version sets the default locale the new one lowers under; a library static shared without --before-classpath; two unrelated RuntimeExceptions, and IllegalArgumentException against a subclass, compared by category; a scope that is false everywhere but sets the default locale before both calls. All five were Verified on the checker at lupovnmv. The order of the calls is observable: with the versions' roles swapped, and with --before-classpath, the shared-static case is a violation.

commits.summary: Countermodels of observed class initializers and of class files the tool read where a JVM reads another: three handed to the evidence stream, two refused
commits.body:
Challenge stream, item 2. lib/tests/fixtures/observed-countermodels holds five fixtures, and lib/tests/observed_countermodels.rs holds each to what a JVM prints. Each was a false proof on the checker as it was (yypzyxmw): crossed, the outside review's A.<clinit> { B.x = 1; k = 7; } (result == 0 proved, a JVM gives 1); lowered, "I".toLowerCase() observed in a Turkish JVM (result == 305 proved, and the locale assumption gone from the result); configured, System.getProperty observed with the property set; released, a class of a multi-release JAR (the tool read the base file where a JVM 17+ loads META-INF/versions/17, so result == 1 was proved where a JVM gives 20, and an observation of the versioned class was put on the base file's code); shadowed, a class path copy of the JDK's org.xml.sax.helpers.AttributesImpl (result == 42 proved, a JVM gives 0).

The first three are the evidence stream's to fix (its brief's item 5 binds an observation): the checker-side test is in the fixtures' README and is sent to its inbox as a failure item. The last two are holes in the class path reader, which no stream owns, so they are refused here: ClassPath::refused (lib/src/classpath.rs) refuses by name, on load and when a class is copied for a pair, a class a multi-release JAR holds a versioned file of, and a class an entry holds in a package of the JDK's image, unless its file is the image's own byte for byte or one of the tool's models (the tool puts both on class paths itself; a first, broader version failed 13 tests for that reason). Enumerating every class still reads the first file, so that walks over which classes exist see it. Not covered: an override only a versioned file declares, and resources.

commits.summary: The challenge stream records its evidence inbox item and a trace error the preservation stream's sync.py put on its line
Countermodels of a checked summary: seven false proofs past the foundation's refusals, refused
commits.body:
Item 3 of the challenge brief. Seven lemmas were proved and their summaries made the checker prove properties a JVM contradicts (fixtures in lib/tests/fixtures/lemma-countermodels, its README has the table).

The first group is an initializer cycle that calls the lemma's method before the final static field it reads is written (seen and heldSeen: proved 7, a JVM gives 0). The foundation's guard looked only at the method's own class.

The second is a final static whose initializer, run by the lemma's proof in the harness's state, reads what a caller changes before it initializes the class: a static (setThenOwn), the default locale (turkishThenLowered) and another class's array (setThenCopied).

The third is a StringBuilder a final static holds, read by the model directly or through a method reference (appendThenLogged and appendThenLoggedThroughLambda). The model's reads never asked Engine::reads.

Summaries are no stream's this run, so they are refused here (lib/src/bmc/mod.rs, strings.rs). No summary is used while any class is being initialized; the call runs as written, so seen and heldSeen are now violations, as on a JVM. Class initializers a lemma's proof runs are held to the lemma's read gate, and objects there when one starts or returns count as there before the call. A lemma reads no StringBuilder that was there before the call.

Tried and found guarded, each with its guard named in the README: a lambda's captured array, the ArrayList model, reflection, self-recursive and mutual lemmas, Pattern and Matcher, model statics, and an induction measure.

Audit: the only lemma in use is PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch (286, 288). It has no statics or initializer, calls only String methods, and is never called from an initializer, so 286's decided result is not affected.

commits.summary: Countermodels of a loop invariant, found guarded; three modelled reads of an array a lemma made no refusal of, refused
commits.body: Item 4 of the challenge brief: seven loops whose late iterations do what the first ones do not (a local written once another reaches 5, statics a callee writes, an array under two names, a relation between two cells, an object reached through an array's cell, nested loops, a 100-cell table at a computed index), in lib/tests/fixtures/loop-countermodels with lib/tests/loop_countermodels.rs. At --unwind 2 none is proved (each is no verdict, its witness spurious, the loop named) and at --unwind 7 late is refuted; the README names what in loops.rs guards each. Reading the array models for it found three false proofs of item 3's kind: a lemma about T.clone()[0], Arrays.copyOf(T, 1)[0] and MessageDigest.isEqual(KEY, {0}) over final static arrays was proved and stood in for a caller that writes the array first (a JVM: 5, 5, 0), since Engine::reads was asked of an array load only. Each, and String.join's array, now refuses an array that was there before the call (mod.rs, bytes.rs, regex.rs); fixtures in lemma-countermodels (Cloned) and a new test in lemma_countermodels.rs. Audit: 287's fixed-guard and fixed-security rest on loop invariants and are not affected; the only lemma in use (simpleMatch, 286/288) reads no array. Verified with test_costs.py run --changed (the whole Rust default tier, 4 of 4 passed) after estimate and tag.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the fresh pair of versions: a scope that writes the caller's array, and two exception classes of one name, each proved to agree
commits.body: Item 5 of the challenge brief, against the preservation stream's zmvkptqz (lib/src/pairing.rs: each version from a fresh state, an exception compared by its class's name). Two pairs of versions a caller tells apart when each runs alone on a JVM are each Verified, non-vacuous, on the preservation line's checker (built apart). first: the scope is called on the caller's own arrays and each version's copy is taken after it, so a scope that zeroes a cell makes the versions agree (alone on {5}: 5 against 0); this line's checker proves it too. failing: two classes named app.Failure, one an IllegalArgumentException and one an IllegalStateException, are one answer by name, though a caller's handler catches one and not the other. Fixtures in lib/tests/fixtures/fresh-pair-countermodels with the commands, the audit and the checker-side test, which fails on both there; lib/tests/fresh_pair_countermodels.rs (tool tier) holds them to a JVM. The pairing is the preservation stream's, so no refusal is committed: the test goes to it as a failure item. Audit: 288-290's allowed changes only read; 289's and 290's accepted preservation answers are already refused by the evidence stream's ymzlyksq until a rerun. Verified: test_costs.py run --changed (default tier, 38 binaries) passed; estimate and tag.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the models on request under assumed gaps: three collections a gap makes, each proved empty where a JVM finds one element
commits.body: Item 5 of the challenge stream, against the state stream's models on request of ArrayDeque and HashSet (kztoupry). Under --gaps assume, a constructor or method a model does not keep makes an object with no field written. The model's size() then reads those fields, though without the model that call has no assume form. The fixture mc.Gapped (lib/tests/fixtures/model-countermodels) has three cases: ArrayDeque.clone(), whose stated assumptions are all true of the JDK; ArrayDeque(Collection); and ArrayList(Collection), which also reproduces on this line. Each is Verified as result == 0 on the state stream's checker (qrqtplwq), and a JVM gives 1. lib/tests/model_countermodels.rs holds the fixture to a JVM. The checker-side test is in the README, where it fails on all three on the state stream's line, and goes to that stream through its inbox, since the models are its this run. The README also lists what was tried and found guarded: the left-out methods under strict, HashSet(int) under advised, a key whose hash changes, a lemma over a deque, and the exception classes. Audit: no example task runs under --gaps assume, so no accepted result is affected. Verified with test_costs.py run --changed (it passed) and the checker-side test run on a copy of the state stream's tree.

commits.summary: Countermodels of a write set: a protected field written before a declared exception, and through one bean passed twice, each proved unchanged
commits.body:
Challenge stream, item 5, against the state stream's write set (qrqtplwq, prove --writes). The frame is conjoined to the assertion, so it is read only after a normal return and only on distinct object inputs. lib/tests/fixtures/frame-countermodels/fc/Framed.java has three methods that a JVM sees writing the protected admin field, each Verified on the state checker built apart at qrqtplwq and at vwktulky. Bean#rename, under --throws 'java.lang.IllegalArgumentException when length < 0', sets admin and then throws. Bean#promote(other), with the write set other.admin, does it when called as b.promote(b). Static grant(from, to), with the write set to.admin, does it when called as grant(b, b). lib/tests/frame_countermodels.rs holds the fixture to a JVM. The README has the table, the commands, the fix options and the checker-side test, which fails on all three on the state line. That test goes to domain-advances-state as a failure item, since the write set is its rule this run, so no refusal is committed here.

Tried and found guarded: a write through a callee, a lambda or a recursion (refuted by the frame); Locale.setDefault (refused by name); a StringBuilder parameter (not taken); an inherited field (fields_of refuses a subclass). The identity of a String field after 16 String operations matches JDK 25 or is a gap. Audit: no example task passes --writes on any line, so no accepted result rests on these holes. Verified with test_costs.py run --changed (passed) and the checker-side test run on both state commits (fails, as it should). Progress also records state-I004, and the evidence session's trace stamps on mqkqvvmw and yypzyxmw for the watcher.

commits.summary: Countermodels of an effect contract at a call: a final static set from a caller's setting, one bean passed twice, and a subclass argument, each a caller's property proved where a JVM breaks it
commits.body:
The state stream's vwktulky lets a setter's checked write set (a lemma with writes:) stand in for its calls through a stub that makes the stated writes. Three callers in lib/tests/fixtures/effect-countermodels each have a proved contract and a property that is Verified on that checker (built apart) while a JVM breaks it. lockedLevel: the setter reads a final static that its class's initializer takes from Config.locked, which the caller sets first, and the contract's proof initialized the class fresh (a JVM gives 0 for 5). pairedLevel: bean.setBoth(bean, mine, theirs) writes the argument's field and then the receiver's, while the stub writes in the writes: order, and the contract's proof never passes one object twice (a JVM gives mine). linkedAdmin: an argument of a subclass whose override, called by the setter, grants admin, since only the receiver's class is checked to be exact.

lib/tests/effect_countermodels.rs holds the fixtures to a JVM. The README has the checker-side test, which fails on all three at vwktulky; it goes to domain-advances-state as a failure item, since the effect contract is that stream's this run, so no refusal is committed here. Also recorded: an exceptional exit does not carry into a caller (throws: is refused, and an undeclared throw refutes the contract, tried), aliasing does, and prove --may-alias this,other already makes the frame refute the earlier promote countermodel. The stub writes a nested object-parameter class with its $, which javac rejects (a refusal). Audit: no example task uses a writes: lemma or --writes on any line. test_costs run --changed and lint pass. The brief is not wrong.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the acceptance check: seven controls accept.py accepts for an answer its evidence does not give
commits.body:
The challenge stream's item 7. Seven controls were written as tests on test_accept.py's own made-up checkout and run against examples/tools/accept.py on the evidence line (krptozvm). Each fails there because accept.py accepts the answer (10 failures with subtests):
- The outcome's target is matched as a substring of the invocation's entry or of an assumption's text. Another method, the same class in another package, and a method an assumption mentions all stand in for the entry.
- The step's driver is any word ending in proofs/prove.py that contains the folder, so a driver of another checkout counts, and so does echo.
- A witness's null inputs are not held to the claim's nullable.
- A witness is not held to the claim's assumption.
- A task's bounds can lower the claim's.
- For a task with no allowed change, the pair is not asked whether it ran with one.
A vacuity witness inside the allowed change is guarded where the task has one (vacuity.outside, ymzlyksq).

The controls, the fix options and the audit are in lib/tests/fixtures/accept-countermodels/README.md. accept.py is the evidence stream's, so nothing in it is changed here, and the controls go to that stream as a failure item.

Audit: given the source commits, the evidence line accepts 13 answers (286, 287, 288, 289, 290), and none rests on these holes. 286 and 287 pass the entry check only by the substring route, through the claim's adapter-entry assumption, so a fix must keep it.

commits.summary: Countermodels of three rules that landed, and three wrong implementations the claims of 287, 307 and 286's protected state accept
Countermodels of an effect contract past its fix: a final field a caller's object was made with, read as if the proof's constructor had made it
commits.body:
The challenge stream's item 5 on the state stream's fixes for its inbox items I005 (sltlykpk, a write set's frame on a declared exceptional exit and over inputs that may be one object) and I007 (nslmqyry, an effect contract reads no non-constant static and stands in only for arguments of exactly their classes). Built apart at nslmqyry, the earlier frame and effect countermodels all pass: both fixes hold.

New hole: inside an effect contract's proof the read gate exempts a final instance field of an object that was there before the call, but the proof makes the receiver and arguments with their constructors in the harness's fresh state, while a caller's object was made in its own. Two callers in lib/tests/fixtures/contract-countermodels (cc.Held) are Verified 'result == level' at nslmqyry, stating no assumption, where a JVM gives 0 for 5: a receiver whose 'final boolean locked = Config.locked' was made with the setting on, and the same through an argument's final field. lib/tests/contract_countermodels.rs holds the fixture to a JVM (tool tier); the checker-side test is in the README and fails on both at nslmqyry, as it should. The effect contract is the state stream's, so nothing in lib/src changes here; it goes to that stream as a failure item. Tried and guarded: a contract whose call starts a class initializer (Engine::initializes_in_frame, the first case of inbox item domain-advances-challenge-I002) and a receiver of a class with two constructors.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the pair of versions past its fix: an exception's interface, message and own field, each proved to agree where a caller's handler tells the versions apart
commits.body:
Challenge stream, item 5, against the preservation stream's wokytpkz (lib/src/pairing.rs: the scope read on copies of its own, an exception compared by its class's name and the names of every class above it). Built apart at wokytpkz with the sources touched, the earlier pairing and fresh-pair countermodel tests pass, checker-side tests included: both fixes hold, and a changed superclass's superclass under kept names is refuted.

New fixture lib/tests/fixtures/thrown-pair-countermodels with lib/tests/thrown_pair_countermodels.rs (tool tier), which holds it to a JVM. Three pairs are each Verified 'agree on every input where k >= 0 && k < 4' at wokytpkz, non-vacuous and with no assumption stated, where a caller's handler tells the versions apart: marked (an interface, the module's documented limit), messaged (the message) and coded (a field of the exception's own class). The README's checker-side test fails on exactly those three there. The pairing is the preservation stream's, so nothing in lib/src changes here; the test goes to it as a failure item.

Audit: 289's and 290's preservation claims say 'throw the same exception'. In their pinned JARs (hashes checked), no class named *Exception or *Error differs between the releases in what it extends, implements or holds (javap -p, 101 and 191 classes), so the interface and field cases cannot occur there. Messages were not compared. Notes are added to both examples. Nothing for the watcher.

Verified with test_costs.py run --changed (all passed) and validate_example.py 289 and 290.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the acceptance check past its fix: a step that goes on past the driver, a step before it, --work given twice and another checker binary, each accepted with no limit
commits.body:
Item 5 and 7 of the challenge brief, against the evidence stream's kqxwrwrx (its fix for domain-advances-evidence-I007). The fix holds: the seven earlier controls in lib/tests/fixtures/accept-countermodels pass against accept.py at kqxwrwrx, and its own test_accept.py passes its 38 tests.

What it leaves is in the step check, which reads a step's words up to the task's name and the first --work, while the pipeline runs the whole step with bash -c and reads nothing else of the job. Four new controls, written against test_accept.py's made-up checkout (DriverRecord), are each accepted with no limit (4 tests, 7 failures with subtests): a shell suffix that rewrites the outcome after the driver; an earlier step that replaces the driver or writes the outcome folder (the driver hash compared is the one the running driver writes); --work given twice (accept.py reads the first, argparse keeps the last, and --work=DIR is not read); and --jvmcontract naming another binary, whose recorded sha256 nothing compares. The README's 'Past the fix' section has the controls' code, the fix options and what was tried and found guarded (a witness on which the assumption throws is unverifiable, not reproduced; a gate over objects is unbound; nulls are JSON null).

accept.py is the evidence stream's, so nothing in it changes here; the controls go to domain-advances-evidence as a failure item citing this commit. Audit: every step of the jobs behind the 13 accepted answers is a plain driver run with one --work, no --jvmcontract and no shell operator, so no accepted answer rests on these holes; nothing for the watcher. Verified by running the controls on an export of the evidence line at kqxwrwrx; test_costs.py run --changed had nothing to run for a README and the brief.

commits.summary: Countermodels of an observed initializer's binding: a lambda replaced by another of its class, an object another class holds, and the default locale, each proved where a JVM says otherwise
commits.body:
The observation binding (evidence's lzpqszyo, copied onto the state line by llyzwmyp, which also names a lambda's hidden class by what it was defined from) compares each class an observed initializer initialized with that class initialized alone, as far as the observation holds its fields, and reads the default locale before the initialization. Three fixtures in lib/tests/fixtures/binding-countermodels (bc), held to a JVM by lib/tests/binding_countermodels.rs (rehooked=5 boxed=5 relocaled=305), are each Verified with --observed-initializer where the checker without the observation finds the violation: rehooked (another class's lambda () -> 1 replaced by its () -> n, both named bc.Hooks$$Lambda since llyzwmyp; proved 1 at state's vvpxytqs, refused at evidence's nsnxmlmt for the lambda's address), boxed (a field of an object another class's final static holds, compared by its class's name; proved 0 at both lines) and relocaled (Locale.setDefault in the initializer; proved 105 at both, every stated assumption reading as true of a JVM that starts in English). The README has the commands, the options for a fix, the checker-side test for the owners and the audit: 290's five observed classes set no locale, time zone or property and write no other class's state, so no accepted result is affected. The binding is evidence's, with a copy on state's line, so nothing in lib/src changes; the test goes to both as failure items.

State's vvpxytqs (an object a JDK call returns under --gaps assume is of a class the engine does not know) holds for an aastore, a string concatenation, a virtual call, a cast and instanceof; a lemma's arguments are primitives and Strings, so no subclass argument reaches one. Also: cost_inventory.python_runs now skips a dotted unittest module that resolves outside the checkout, as it already did for a file path; test_costs.py estimate failed on this session's log of a run in a /tmp export without it. Verified: test_costs.py run --changed passed (45 Rust binaries, the Python suites). The brief's other sections are still accurate.

commits.summary: Countermodels of an effect contract's stub inside a proof that limits writes: a proof by induction and an empty write set, each proved where a JVM writes what they rule out
commits.body:
Answers the challenge stream's inbox item I002 (where the lemma rule and the state stream's write-set rule meet in Engine::call). The two cases it names cannot occur: a lemma's proof and an effect contract's proof are given no lemma and no contract (lemmas: None in property.rs), so a framed or contracted call inside them runs as written and Engine::keeps sees it. What does occur is a check's own --decreases or --writes with an effect contract in --lemmas: the stub's effect intrinsic puts each written field into the object directly, without asking keeps.

lib/tests/fixtures/stub-countermodels holds two: Store.f, proved by induction on k, writes a static's bean through a contracted setter, calls itself and reads the bean, and result == 0 is Verified while a JVM gives f(2) == -1 (the hypothesis drops the call's write); Touch.touch with --writes '' writes a static's bean through the setter and is Verified, with a statement that says nothing of the write set. Both are Verified on state's twtuqvvr and on a trial merge of this line with state's vvpxytqs, each built apart, and both are refused there without the contract. lib/tests/stub_countermodels.rs holds the fixture to a JVM; the README has the checker-side test for the state stream, which owns effect contracts, so nothing in lib/src changes here. Audit: no example's decreases: is in a check that takes a contract, and none has writes: or --writes. test_costs.py run --changed passed.

commits.summary: Countermodels of what the pair of versions takes as the same code: a loop's ties and the identical-bytecode shortcut, each proved where a JVM tells the versions apart
commits.body:
Item 5 of the challenge brief, against the preservation stream's owrsowqm (lib/src/bmc/ties.rs). In a pair of versions, two summaries of one loop take one set of free bits where the code and the state are the same. Both rest on reach in lib/src/shared.rs, and so does the older shortcut that verifies a target identical in both versions with nothing to prove. reach follows no call whose owner is a JDK class or interface, so an application class's code run through IntUnaryOperator is in no fingerprint. A class's surface for the key also leaves out its private methods, and a class only that code reads is not in uses, so its statics are not in the key.

lib/tests/fixtures/tie-countermodels: the old and new versions differ only in Step's private helper and Config's initializer, and a JVM gives 2 against 1 past 1000 (lib/tests/tie_countermodels.rs). At preservation's lmyvttyt, built apart, summed and configured are each Verified to agree on k < 2000 at --unwind 2, non-vacuous and with no assumption. On this line, without the ties, both get no verdict. supplied under the defaults is 'behaves as before on every input (identical in both versions; nothing to prove)' on every line, this one included. The README's checker-side test fails on all three at lmyvttyt. The pairing and shared.rs are preservation's this run, so nothing in lib/src changes here; the test goes to it as a failure item.

commits.summary: Countermodels of an observation bound to the settings it read: a property read under a JDK frame or through putIfAbsent, the environment by a looked-up handle, and three startup settings, each proved where a JVM under another setting says otherwise
commits.body:
Item 5 against the evidence stream's mmnoqopr (its fix for I008) and vqquvmnm (its fix for I011). Both hold. Built apart with the sources touched, observed_countermodels.rs passes at qxstltmq and at vqquvmnm, and I011's test passes at vqquvmnm. Six initializers read a setting the binding does not see, and each is Verified at vqquvmnm with the class observed under that setting. The result says 'it read no system property' and nothing of the setting. The cases: a property read through Optional.map(System::getProperty), where the lambda's frame is hidden so the recorder takes the JDK's Optional for the reader; the value Properties.putIfAbsent returns, which Recording does not override; getenv through a method handle looked up by name; and the processor count, the working directory and the default charset, which the JDK reads at startup. lib/tests/setting_countermodels.rs holds each case to a JVM, under the setting and under another. The checker-side test is in lib/tests/fixtures/setting-countermodels/README.md, and it fails on all six at vqquvmnm; it goes to the evidence stream as a failure item. Nothing in lib/src changes.

Audit: 290's five observed classes (hash-checked JARs, javap -c -p) call none of these methods. UrlPathHelper's logger reaches JUL's configuration through JDK frames, but the observation does not hold the logger, so a read of it is refused. No accepted result is affected.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the code two versions are taken to share past the reach's fix: an override removed, a hidden field, an interface's initializer two ways and the target's own class's, each taken as identical or tied where a JVM tells the versions apart
commits.body:
Item 5 of the challenge brief, against the preservation stream's kskmpmny (its fix for domain-advances-preservation-I010). The fix holds: built apart with the sources touched, tie_countermodels.rs passes there, its checker-side test included. Past it, lib/src/shared.rs's reach still leaves out five things, each shown by lib/tests/fixtures/reach-countermodels (old/ against new/), where each version alone gives 2 (0 for hidden) against 1 on a JVM (lib/tests/reach_countermodels.rs). Under the defaults, each of these is 'identical in both versions; nothing to prove' at kskmpmny and on this line alike, since the shortcut is older than the run: removed (an override the previous version declared and the new one inherits; only the new version's reach is walked and the old one is looked up by the new one's declaring class), hidden (a field the previous version declared that hides an inherited one; fields are not compared), constant (an interface's static read through an implementing class; the JVM initializes the interface, initialized() takes superclasses only), defaulted (making an object initializes a superinterface with a default method) and Own#f (the target's own class's initializer). looped, constant's read in a loop past the bound, is Verified under the ties at kskmpmny, non-vacuous; on this line it gets no verdict.

shared.rs is the preservation stream's this run, so nothing in lib/src changes here: the README's checker-side test, which fails on all six at kskmpmny, goes to it as a failure item citing this commit. Audit: the shortcut needs no --before-classpath, which 288 to 290 all pass; 289's rerun on kskmpmny unwinds fully; 287's BCrypt implements no interface and uses only its own fields in both pinned releases. No accepted result is affected. Inbox I004 is acknowledged as waiting: preservation's call-level rule is not committed yet. Verified: the changed tests under MemoryMax=8G with --rust-jobs 1 passed after test_costs.py estimate and tag; lint agrees.

commits.summary: Countermodels of a stand-in a lemma's proof rested on, and of an Error a logged record's getter raises with no athrow, each proved with nothing stated where a JVM says otherwise
commits.body: Item 5 of the challenge brief, against state's stand-ins (qlylowvo, prove --stand-in) and preservation's logging fix (lqkwokqq). A lemma's proof is a check of its own, given the check's stand-ins. The check that uses the lemma states the lemma as proved, and states only what its own run's engine noted. So at state's zlvqxmst, built apart, sn.Use#viaLemma is Verified through a lemma whose proof called a narrowly sampled stand-in, and its result names no stand-in; a JVM gives 32 where 0 is proved (lib/tests/fixtures/stand-in-countermodels). A model on request is lost the same way. Preservation's scan refuses athrow in a logged record's classes, but a JVM raises an Error without one: an OutOfMemoryError (new long[Integer.MAX_VALUE]) and a StackOverflowError (a recursion) in getMessage() each leave log through StreamHandler.publish's catch (Exception). Both are Verified 'log returned' at kskmpmny (lib/tests/fixtures/log-countermodels). The rules are those streams', so nothing in lib/src changes; each README has the checker-side test, which goes to the owner as a failure item. No accepted result rests on either: 286's simpleMatch lemma calls only String methods, and 287's LocationResolvingLogRecord neither recurses nor allocates by input.

commits.summary: Countermodels of the code two versions are taken to share past the reach's second fix: a superclass, an interface and a default method's interface changed under identical code, each taken as identical or tied where a JVM tells the versions apart
commits.body: Item 5 of the challenge stream, against the preservation stream's qopxypnn (its fix for domain-advances-preservation-I019). The fix holds for what it was made for: built apart at qopxypnn with the sources touched, reach_countermodels.rs passes, its checker-side test included. What shared::reach still never compares is a class's header, its superclass and its interfaces. same_everywhere also checks only that each method one version reaches exists, the same, in the other, not that both reach the same methods. The new fixture lib/tests/fixtures/supertype-countermodels has old/ and new/ versions in which every method of every class is the same text and only three class headers differ. Under the defaults, four targets are 'identical in both versions; nothing to prove' at qopxypnn and on this line alike: rebased (Child.value resolves to One.value, then to Two.value), marked (instanceof of an interface the previous Plain implements), cast (the same checkcast, which throws in the new version) and mixed (a default method from Left, then from Right). looped (marked in a loop past the bound) is Verified under the ties, non-vacuous. A JVM gives 2 against 1 (or a ClassCastException) for each. With the shortcut turned off, three are refuted, and looped is refuted at full unwind, so only the shortcut and the ties are wrong. The README has the table, the commands, the fix options and a checker-side test, which fails on all five at qopxypnn. shared.rs is preservation's this run, so nothing in lib/src changes here; the test goes to that stream as a failure item. lib/tests/supertype_countermodels.rs holds the fixture to a JVM.

commits.summary: Countermodels of a call taken as one function of both versions: cells a JDK method writes, a String's identity and an Error the JVM raises, each proved to agree where a JVM tells the versions apart
commits.body:
Item 5 and inbox item I004 of the domain-advances challenge stream. The preservation stream's call-level rule (uxyusvsv, xuwlklyo; lib/src/bmc/ties.rs and shared::one_function) takes a call of code both versions share as a function of its inputs. Built apart at qmsonuow with the sources touched, on JDK 25.0.5, the I004 floor holds: callee-countermodels' check.py proves no countermodel, and same, copied and parsed verify.

Past it, lib/tests/fixtures/function-countermodels has seven pairs whose Shared class is the same bytes in both versions. Each is Verified under --assume 'k >= 0', non-vacuous, where each version run alone on a JVM gives another answer: filled and copied (the callee writes an argument only through Arrays.fill or System.arraycopy, and writes_arrays looks only for an array store of the application's own); interned (the callee tests s == "key", and the inputs name a String by its content); same and tagged (two related calls return one object, and a returned literal is never the literal); overflowed and exhausted (no Error is among the outcomes, so two handlers of a StackOverflowError or an OutOfMemoryError are never reached). In a scratch copy with the rule off, none is proved. hashed, encoded and messaged were tried and are guarded (the reach left open, or a gap), and stay as controls. lib/tests/function_countermodels.rs holds every pair to a JVM; the fixtures' README has the checker-side test, which fails on exactly the seven at qmsonuow, and the options.

Also found: --no-shared-callees does not turn the rule off, though its help says it proves each callee as written. Nothing passes it to bmc::Options::calls_as_one_function. The rule is preservation's, so nothing in lib/src changes here; the test goes to that stream as a failure item. Audit: 287's accepted preservation and 307's tasks rest on the rule, but their BCrypt (read from hash-checked JARs and slices) has no identity test, no JDK array writer and no recursion, and no caller catches an Error, so they are not affected. Preservation's sqprlwkv (its fixes for I021 and I022) holds: the log, supertype and reach countermodel tests pass at qmsonuow. Verified with test_costs.py run --changed under an 8G cap, the new test and tiers.rs run alone, estimate, tag and lint.

commits.summary: Countermodels of an exception's message kept from its constructor: a model of the JDK that throws the JDK's exception with another message, each proved to have none where a JVM gives the JDK's
commits.body:
Item 5 and inbox item domain-advances-challenge-I005: the state stream's last rules, at its final commit kmytvuop, built apart with the sources touched. Its fix for I017 (plplrxrt, a check through a lemma states what the lemma's proof rested on) holds: stand_in_countermodels.rs and state's own checker-side test pass there. Its vwrmzmst keeps a JDK exception's message and cause from the constructor the engine ran, and models getMessage, getLocalizedMessage, getCause and toString from them. The engine runs its models of JDK classes (lib/models) as bytecode, and two of them throw the JDK's exception class with another message: ImmutableCollections.List12.get past its end throws new IndexOutOfBoundsException() where the JDK says 'Index: 2 Size: 1', and HashMap(int) of a negative capacity throws new IllegalArgumentException() where the JDK says 'Illegal initial capacity: -1'. Four methods of lib/tests/fixtures/throwable-countermodels/tm/Thrown.java are each Verified at kmytvuop, non-vacuous, with nothing stated beyond the assumption and JDK initialization: the message proved null, the toString proved 35 units long (53 on a JVM), the localized message proved null (28 units). On this line's checker, without the rule, each stops at the gap of the message method.

The rule is the state stream's, so nothing in lib/src changes here: the checker-side test is in the fixture's README and goes to domain-advances-state as a failure item. lib/tests/throwable_countermodels.rs holds the fixture to a JVM. No accepted result rests on the rule (286's fixed task is not decided, and 288's 6.1.14 proof is no task). Verified: test_costs.py run --changed under an 8G cap with one Rust job passed; after estimate and tag the new test file, tiers.rs and lint pass; the README's checker-side test fails on all four at kmytvuop, as it should.
